fatal_blockers: No proposal currently establishes the FRONTIER lemma. The obstruction audits are design promises, not evidence of equal completeness, transfer closure, unrestricted separation, or λ/μ≥65/64; none implies recursion or GapCVP hardness.

Proposal 2 is not a bounded search because denominator-bounded couplings have no numerator, scale, or compact Gram bound. Construction-A decoding separates cosets but does not charge same-coset affine collisions, signed combinations, DROP, or prove adverse transfer growth.

Proposal 3 leaves the ideal, label search range, and coupling family unspecified, so its experiment is not finite. Total positivity and multiple embeddings give coercivity only at infinity; they do not exclude short unit translates or trace-balanced affine combinations inside the legal sphere.

Proposal 4 is killed as written: unimodularity excludes nonvertex lattice points from an alcove simplex but does not itself make a selected legal subset an empty cospherical Delaunay set. Its proposed first glued table also falls short of complete NAND/COPY depth-two closure and unrestricted λ/μ certification.

Proposal 5 is not executable as bounded: “normalized rational Grams” remains infinite without denominator, height, eigenvalue, and compactness bounds. Farkas certificates over a generated finite competitor set do not certify all lattice points unless termination is proved by a uniform ellipsoid bound.

Proposal 6 is structurally blocked as stated by cut submodularity. Equal globally minimal legal NAND cuts would force uncrossed meet/join cuts to be equally cheap; the NAND relation is not closed under these operations, and minimizing over auxiliary cut vertices preserves submodularity.

Proposal 1 alone escapes the verified antipodal midpoint obstruction, but failure modes include unequal legal radii, any extra point on or inside the sphere, transfer nonclosure, control mismatch, or λ/μ<65/64—not merely a three-point affine combination. A negative result would reject only the retained non-antipodal D4/Gram grid, not arbitrary Voronoi tiles.

Exact positive-definite ellipsoid bounds plus enumeration of every lattice point through the incumbent radius can provide a global certificate over all integers. Named attacks or a finite shell without such a proved bound would repeat G2/G3/G14/G31/G38.
